promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 3 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Welcome back, and sorry about the fortnight you've just had. We pick up a notch below where you left off, keep three short walk-runs, and shift the goal to finishing the 5K strong, with running the whole way as a stretch rather than the headline.

flags.title: Returning from two weeks off
flags.detail: start a shade easier than before the break, not from zero.

flags.title: Sleep and stress
flags.detail: six hours and a lot going on, so recovery is thin and we keep efforts gentle.

flags.title: Goal is tight
flags.detail: longest run segment so far is 2 minutes, so running an unbroken 5K in four weeks is a stretch.

flags.title: Three missed sessions
flags.detail: the week was lost to your mum, not to training choices, so no correction needed.

answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
No, you do not start from the beginning. Two weeks off takes a little edge off your fitness, not all of it. We drop the first run of the week by one interval, hold the middle one at where you were, and nudge the Saturday one a step forward. By the end of this week you will be back on track.

On the 5K being four weeks away: finishing it is realistic, and I would bet on you to do that well. Running every step without walking is honest-to-God a stretch, because your longest unbroken run so far is 2 minutes and the race takes roughly 40. We will push toward longer run intervals over the next three weeks and see how your body answers. If we get there, brilliant; if not, finishing with a few short walk breaks is a real win for someone eight weeks into running.

new.analysis:
The plan is a gentle re-entry, not a restart. Monday eases in with one fewer run interval than before the break, Wednesday matches what you were doing, and Saturday starts stretching the run segments from 2 minutes to 3. That gives your legs a kind landing and still moves the needle toward a continuous 5K.

The reason for the small step back is two weeks off plus six hours of sleep and a lot on your plate. Jumping straight to the hardest session you had done would raise the risk of a niggle at exactly the wrong moment. One slightly easier Monday buys the rest of the week.

The bigger picture is that we had hoped to be in a sharpening phase by now, and instead we are rebuilding. That is fine, and it changes what "success" looks like on Nov 15. Over the next three weeks I will keep lengthening the run portions each Saturday, aiming for 5 and then 8 minutes of continuous running, so that race day feels familiar rather than new.

One ask: on each run, keep the running portion at a pace where you could say a short sentence. If you cannot, slow it down. The walk breaks are there to let the next run interval feel repeatable, not to recover from a sprint.
